answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: 1955–2011 · Co-founder of Apple & NeXT, chairman of Pixar
answer.sourceLine: Credited to Jobs on essentially every quote site, and squarely in character for the man who ran the Macintosh team. But no primary source pins this wording to him: Wikiquote keeps it in its unsourced pile, and the only citation trail we could follow is a 2011 quote compilation that points back to Jeffrey S. Young’s 1987 biography — a page reference nobody has produced.

source.excerpt: People judge you by your performance, so focus on the outcome. Be a yardstick of quality. Some people aren’t used to an environment where excellence is expected.
trail: Wikiquote’s Talk:Steve Jobs ↗ page carries this exact sentence in its “Unsourced” section, opened by an editor in March 2009 with the note that Wikiquote no longer allows unsourced quotations. It is still sitting there — nobody has produced the reliable, precise source that would move it across.
It is correspondingly absent from the sourced Wikiquote article on Steve Jobs ↗, which is where quotations go once a citation is verified.

George Beahm’s 2011 collection I, Steve: Steve Jobs in His Own Words ↗ prints the three-sentence form under the heading “Excellence” and appends a source line pointing to Jeffrey S. Young’s 1987 biography. That is the closest thing to a citation anyone offers.

Young’s Steve Jobs: The Journey Is the Reward ↗ is a real book — Scott, Foresman, first published 1987 — but the Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted and we could not search inside it, so we treat that page reference as unconfirmed rather than repeat it as fact.
source.excerptNote: The fuller three-sentence form as printed in George Beahm’s 2011 compilation, under the heading “Excellence.” The popular one-line version drops the opening sentence.

author.bio: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in 1976, was pushed out in the mid-1980s, built NeXT and bankrolled Pixar, then returned to Apple in 1997 to oversee the iMac, iPod, iPhone and iPad. His reputation for demanding excellence — and for being brutal about it — is exactly why lines like this one stick to him so easily. He died on 5 October 2011, after which quote collections about him multiplied faster than anyone could source them.

misattribution.heading: Sources it gets pinned to that don’t hold
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Jobs himself may well be right. The sources attached to it online are the problem — two circulate widely and neither survives a look.

items.why: Several sites tie the line to Jobs’s 2008 Fortune interview with Betsy Morris. The published transcript of that interview ↗ contains neither “yardstick” nor “excellence is expected.” The likeliest explanation is a misread of Beahm’s compilation, where the CNNMoney credit belongs to the quotation printed immediately before this one.

items.who: Motivating Thoughts of Steve Jobs (Prabhat Prakashan)
items.why: LibQuotes ↗ cites a modern quote anthology as the source. Anthologies of this kind reprint from other anthologies; citing one tells you the line was in circulation, not where it came from.

As printed in Beahm’s collection ↗ the passage opens “People judge you by your performance, so focus on the outcome” before reaching the yardstick line. The version that travels online is a trimmed excerpt.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest position: the sentiment and the phrasing are entirely Jobs-like, no rival claimant exists, and Wikiquote’s editors have nonetheless left it in the unsourced pile ↗ since 2009. Credit it to Jobs if you like — but do not attach a date or an interview to it.

context.heading: Why this one is hard to pin down
lead: Jobs is one of the most heavily quoted people of the last half-century, and most of the famous lines have receipts: the Stanford commencement address is on video, the Playboy and Fortune interviews are transcribed, the internal Apple memos have been reproduced. This sentence has none of that — it surfaces fully formed in quote collections, without a stage, a date or an interviewer attached.

That pattern is the signature of a line that entered circulation through a compilation rather than a recording. It does not make the quote false. It does mean that anyone citing it with a confident year is citing the compilation, not Jobs.
context.pull: No stage, no date, no interviewer — just the sentence.
